fact: The 'end of the river' — spinning so fast it is squashed into the sky's most flattened star.
bio: Achernar (Alpha Eridani) is a hot blue star about 139 light-years away marking the southern end of the celestial river Eridanus. It rotates near its break-up speed, bulging so strongly at the equator that its diameter there is roughly half again its polar diameter — the most oblate star known among the bright ones.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the end of the river'. Lying deep in the southern sky, it was invisible to the classical Mediterranean astronomers and entered star charts only with the age of southern-hemisphere exploration.
